newsitem.title: UK: Britain to crackdown on "Alcopops" aimed at teens.
newsitem.headline: Britain to crackdown on "Alcopops" aimed at teens.

text.p: Britain is to crack down on teenage drinking by targeting alcoholic sodas known as "alcopops", which manufacturers have been accused of aiming deliberately at youngsters.
Government sources said on Wednesday ministers would announce measures on Thursday to detect shopkeepers and bar-owners who sell the products, with names such as Hooch and Two Dogs, to under-18s.
Home Secretary (interior minister) Jack Straw ordered an inquiry into alcopops two weeks after the new Labour government took office.
He was backed up by a judge who described alcopop makers as "grossly irresponsible" after he heard how a 14-year-old boy got drunk on alcoholic lemonade and cider, and then burned down a school.
The tabloid Sun newspaper said on Wednesday the government planned to encourage local councils to hire teenage "spies" to test whether shops would sell them alcohol.

It said that under other measures to be announced, shopkeepers and other offenders would risk losing their liquor licences and young people wanting to buy alcohol would have to carry identity cards to show they were over 18.
